step: Employer applies for employee work entry permit via MOI / Ministry of Labour portal
authority: Ministry of Interior (MOI) and Ministry of Labour (ADLSA)
field_label: Employee nationality, passport number, approved profession code, employer commercial registration number
deadline_label: Minimum 4 weeks before intended arrival date

step: Employee attends Qatar Visa Centre (QVC) for pre-arrival medical examination and biometric capture
authority: Qatar Visa Centre / Ministry of Interior
field_label: Biometric data capture, blood test, chest X-ray, document verification at QVC in home country
deadline_label: Must be completed before boarding Qatar-bound flight; allow 2 weeks minimum
non_obvious_official_guidance: Workers of eligible nationalities must attend a Qatar Visa Centre in their home country before travelling; the entry permit is only activated after QVC clearance is confirmed.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Workers from India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Philippines, Indonesia, Kenya, and Ethiopia (among others) MUST attend a QVC or they cannot board a Qatar-bound flight — the entry permit is not activated in the airline system without QVC clearance. Many HR generalists issue travel authorisation without checking QVC nationality eligibility, resulting in the employee being denied boarding.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm employee nationality against the current QVC country list before issuing any travel authorisation. QVC attendance cannot be substituted or waived by the employer. Book the QVC appointment as soon as the entry permit is approved.
source: Hukoomi Qatar e-Government Portal — Qatar Visa Centre

step: Obtain and attest police clearance certificate from home country for regulated professions and selected nationalities
authority: Home country police authority and Qatar Ministry of Interior
field_label: Full legal name, passport number, period and country of residence
deadline_label: Before entry permit application; allow 4 weeks for apostille and attestation chain
non_obvious_official_guidance: Criminal record clearance may be required as part of the entry permit or residence permit process for certain nationalities and professions.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Healthcare workers, educators, financial sector employees, and security personnel are routinely required to submit a police clearance. The certificate must be authenticated by the home country Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then the Qatar Embassy — a chain that adds 2–4 weeks. HR teams that discover this requirement after the entry permit is already issued face significant departure delays.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm with the employer's PRO or immigration agent whether a police clearance is required for the specific nationality and profession code before initiating the entry permit application. Start the attestation chain immediately if required.

step: Register employment contract on Ministry of Labour (ADLSA) portal before employee travels to Qatar
field_label: Job title matching approved profession code, basic salary, total package, working hours, accommodation provision, contract term
deadline_label: Before or concurrent with entry permit application
non_obvious_official_guidance: All employment contracts for expatriate workers must be registered with the Ministry of Labour before the worker travels to Qatar.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The job title on the registered contract must exactly match the profession code approved on the entry permit. Mismatches flag the system and can block the residence permit application. HR generalists frequently use internally preferred job titles that do not correspond to the official ADLSA profession code list.
non_obvious_action_required: Cross-check the profession code on the approved entry permit against the job title in the employment contract before registration. Use the official ADLSA profession code description verbatim — not an internal HR title.
source: Ministry of Labour Qatar (ADLSA) — Labour Law

step: Complete in-country medical commission examination at MOH-approved facility
authority: Ministry of Public Health / Hamad Medical Corporation
field_label: Blood test, chest X-ray, general physical examination, infectious disease screening
deadline_label: Within first 3 days of arrival; required before QID application can be submitted
non_obvious_official_guidance: All expatriate workers must pass a medical fitness examination conducted at a Ministry of Public Health-approved medical commission centre in Qatar.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A failed in-country medical (e.g. active tuberculosis, HIV, Hepatitis B/C) results in immediate deportation. This can occur even if the employee passed the QVC pre-arrival medical — in-country testing uses different protocols and the ruling is final with no appeal process for the employer. Non-refundable accommodation leases or international freight shipments signed before QID issuance carry this risk.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief employees explicitly that a second independent medical occurs in-country and failure means repatriation. Do not book non-refundable shipping, school enrolment, or annual housing leases until the QID is confirmed as issued.
source: Ministry of Interior Qatar — Residence Permit Services

step: Provide biometric fingerprints and photograph at MOI service centre
field_label: Ten-finger biometric scan, facial photograph at MOI Fingerprinting Centre
deadline_label: Concurrent with medical commission process; within first week of arrival

step: Employer PRO submits Residence Permit / Qatar ID application at MOI on behalf of employee
field_label: Passport, entry permit number, medical fitness clearance, registered employment contract, employer stamp and QID
deadline_label: Within entry permit validity period — typically 30 to 90 days from arrival date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees must obtain a Residence Permit within the validity period of their entry permit.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The Qatar ID (QID) card IS the Residence Permit — Qatar does not issue a separate RP sticker or stamp in the passport as the UAE and Saudi Arabia do. HR generalists accustomed to those countries expect a passport endorsement and may incorrectly tell employees they are waiting for something additional. The passport receives no residency marking.
non_obvious_action_required: Inform employees and family members explicitly that the QID smart card is the sole document evidencing legal residence in Qatar. It must be carried at all times and is required for healthcare, banking, government services, and travel through Qatar airports.
source: Ministry of Interior Qatar — Residence Permit Services

step: Collect Qatar ID (QID) card from MOI service centre or authorised collection point
field_label: Application reference number, employee original passport for verification
deadline_label: Typically 7–14 working days after RP application submission

step: Register on Metrash2 MOI mobile application to access e-government immigration services
field_label: QID number, Qatar-registered mobile number, email address, OTP verification
deadline_label: Immediately after QID issuance; no regulatory deadline but required for all self-service MOI transactions
non_obvious_official_guidance: Metrash2 is the official Ministry of Interior mobile application providing access to over 50 e-services including residence permit renewal, sponsorship transfers, and traffic inquiries.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Metrash2 is the primary channel for RP renewals, dependant sponsorship applications, and vehicle-related transactions. Without it, every MOI transaction requires physical attendance at a service centre with long wait times. HR teams that omit Metrash2 from Day 1 onboarding create an avoidable ongoing queue burden for both employees and the PRO team.
non_obvious_action_required: Add Metrash2 registration to the Day 1 onboarding checklist. The app requires the QID number so it cannot be set up before QID issuance. Ensure the employee uses a Qatar-registered SIM for the mandatory OTP verification step.

step: Register on Hukoomi Qatar e-government portal for access to multi-ministry digital services
authority: Government of Qatar / Ministry of Interior
field_label: QID number, Qatar mobile number, email address
deadline_label: After QID issuance; no regulatory deadline

step: Obtain Health Card and register with Primary Health Care Corporation (PHCC) health centre
authority: Ministry of Public Health / Primary Health Care Corporation (PHCC)
field_label: QID, passport copy, employer confirmation letter
deadline_label: Within first month; required before accessing state healthcare system
non_obvious_official_guidance: Expatriates holding a valid QID may apply for a Health Card to access Hamad Medical Corporation hospitals and PHCC primary health centres.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The state Health Card covers Hamad Medical Corporation and PHCC facilities only — private hospitals are not included. Some employers do not provide private health insurance and represent the Health Card as equivalent coverage. Employees who assume 'employer-provided healthcare' means private hospital access face unexpected out-of-pocket costs for specialist or elective care.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm explicitly with the employer at offer stage whether private health insurance is included in the package or only the state Health Card. If only the state Health Card is provided, budget for private out-of-pocket costs for any care outside the Hamad/PHCC network.

step: Open Qatar-registered bank account to receive WPS salary payments before first payroll cycle
field_label: QID, passport, employer salary certificate or offer letter, proof of Qatar address
deadline_label: Before first payroll cycle; aim for within 21 days of arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: Wages under the Wage Protection System (WPS) must be paid to a Qatar-registered bank account in the employee's name.
non_obvious_actual_reality: WPS transfers can only clear into a local Qatar bank account. Employees without one may have salary held or paid by cheque, creating a WPS compliance failure for the employer. Some banks require three months of payslips from new customers — creating a deadlock for new arrivals. An employer offer letter is accepted as a substitute by most banks when presented with the QID.
non_obvious_action_required: HR should confirm which bank(s) the employer's payroll uses for WPS and whether a facilitated account-opening arrangement exists for new joiners. Include bank account setup in the first-week onboarding checklist alongside QID collection.

step: Employer ensures all private sector wages are paid through the Wage Protection System (WPS) within statutory deadline
field_label: Monthly wage amount, WPS transfer date, WPS confirmation reference number
deadline_label: Within 7 days of the contractual pay date each month
non_obvious_official_guidance: All private sector employers must pay wages through the Wage Protection System. Wages not transferred within the statutory deadline constitute a violation of Qatar Labour Law.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A single missed WPS deadline automatically blacklists the employer across all government systems with immediate effect — no advance warning is given. New work permits, RP renewals, and all MOI/MOL transactions are blocked for the entire company until the violation is resolved. Non-Qatari correspondent banks can introduce clearing delays that produce violations even when the employer initiated the transfer on time.
non_obvious_action_required: Schedule WPS payroll transfers to clear at least 3 business days before the contractual pay date. Confirm with the company bank that WPS transfers settle on the same business day they are sent. Maintain a monthly log of WPS receipt confirmations as evidence in any dispute.
source: Ministry of Labour Qatar — Wage Protection System

step: Calculate and pay end-of-service gratuity to employee on contract termination, resignation, or expiry
field_label: Basic salary figure, completed full years of service, gratuity calculation worksheet
deadline_label: Payable within 7 days of contract end date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Qatar Labour Law No. 14 of 2004, Article 54: employees are entitled to end-of-service gratuity of not less than three weeks' remuneration for each year of service completed.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The three-week calculation is based on BASIC salary only — housing allowance, transport allowance, and other package elements are excluded. Many employees calculate expected gratuity on gross salary and receive a significantly lower payout at departure. The entitlement applies from the first year of service regardless of whether the employee resigned — employers who withhold gratuity from employees who resign before five years are acting unlawfully under Qatari law.
non_obvious_action_required: Employees should request a written gratuity calculation before signing any termination or separation agreement. Verify the employer is using basic salary as the base, not gross, and confirm the calculation at the conclusion of each contract year.
source: Ministry of Labour Qatar — Labour Law No. 14 of 2004

step: Confirm no personal income tax obligation in Qatar; obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from GTA if home-country treaty relief is required
field_label: QID, proof of Qatar residence over 183 days, passport, employer letter confirming employment dates, utility bill or lease agreement
deadline_label: On request; no statutory Qatar filing deadline for individuals
non_obvious_official_guidance: Qatar does not levy personal income tax on individuals. The General Tax Authority issues Tax Residency Certificates to qualifying residents who have been physically present in Qatar for at least 183 days in a calendar year and have a permanent home in Qatar.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Qatar has no personal income tax, but employees may remain tax residents of their home country and owe tax there on Qatar-sourced income depending on domestic rules and applicable double taxation treaty provisions. HR teams that tell employees 'there is no tax in Qatar' without flagging home-country obligations can create serious personal tax exposure. The TRC is needed to claim treaty relief in the home country but requires 183+ days of physical presence and a permanent Qatar home — newly arrived employees often do not yet qualify.
non_obvious_action_required: HR must not give tax advice on home-country obligations. Advise all employees to take independent personal tax advice in their home country before departure. Provide signed employer letters confirming Qatar employment start and end dates to support the employee's home-country tax filings.

step: Confirm no expatriate social security contribution requirement in Qatar; review home-country pension and social security position
field_label: N/A — no contribution form or registration required for expatriate employees
non_obvious_official_guidance: Qatar's social insurance system (Law No. 24 of 2002) applies exclusively to Qatari nationals. Expatriate employees do not contribute to and do not accrue entitlements under the Qatari state social security or pension system.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Expatriate employees in Qatar receive no state pension, unemployment insurance, or social security protection from Qatar. End-of-service gratuity is the only mandatory post-employment financial protection. Qatar has signed very few bilateral social security totalization agreements — employees from EU/EEA countries should not assume that years worked in Qatar count toward their home-country pension entitlement. This gap is routinely not disclosed at offer stage.
non_obvious_action_required: Employees planning a multi-year Qatar assignment should obtain home-country pension and social security advice before departure and consider voluntary contributions or private savings to cover the Qatar period. HR should flag the absence of Qatar social security coverage proactively at the offer stage.
source: Ministry of Labour Qatar — Labour Law

step: Employee sponsors dependants (spouse, children) for family residence permits via MOI after own QID is issued
field_label: Employee QID, dependant passports, attested marriage and birth certificates, employer salary certificate confirming total package
deadline_label: After employee QID issuance; apply before dependants travel to Qatar
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees holding a valid Qatar residence permit may sponsor immediate family members for residence permits subject to meeting a minimum monthly salary requirement set by the Ministry of Interior.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The minimum salary to sponsor a spouse is approximately QAR 7,000 per month; lower thresholds apply for sponsoring children only. These thresholds are not clearly published on official portals and have changed without formal advance notice. Employees earning below the threshold have no legal pathway to bring family to Qatar — a fact that must be disclosed at offer stage, not after the employee has relocated alone. Marriage and birth certificates must be attested by the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Qatar Embassy before MOI will accept them.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm the employee's total monthly package meets the sponsorship salary threshold before the offer is accepted or family is given notice of moving. Begin the attestation chain — home-country apostille, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Qatar Embassy — for all family documents at least 8 weeks before the planned family arrival date.
source: Ministry of Interior Qatar — Family Residence Permit

step: Renew Qatar ID (Residence Permit) before expiry; employer PRO responsible for timely submission
field_label: Current QID number, renewed or extended employment contract, updated medical clearance if required by MOI
deadline_label: Apply minimum 30 days before QID expiry date; no grace period after expiry
non_obvious_official_guidance: Residence permits must be renewed before their expiry date. Allowing a residence permit to lapse is a violation of Qatari immigration law.
non_obvious_actual_reality: An expired QID creates an immigration overstay violation the moment it lapses — there is no grace period in Qatar. Overstay fines accrue from the day of expiry and the employee becomes immediately deportable. The employer is legally responsible for timely renewal. WPS compliance is automatically verified during the renewal process and any missed wage payment blocks the renewal for the entire company.
non_obvious_action_required: Set automated calendar alerts at 60 and 30 days before every employee's QID expiry date. Confirm WPS compliance is clean before initiating renewal. Verify no MOL or MOI blacklisting flags are outstanding on the company account before the first renewal submission.
source: Ministry of Interior Qatar — Residence Permit Renewal

step: Transfer employment sponsorship to new employer after completing statutory service period under kafala reform
authority: Ministry of Labour (ADLSA) and Ministry of Interior
field_label: Current QID, current employer commercial registration, new employer commercial registration, proof of 1-year completed service
deadline_label: After 1 full year of continuous service with current employer (or immediately in qualifying circumstances)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Qatar Labour Law reform implemented via Ministerial Decision No. 51 of 2020 allows workers to change employers without current employer consent after completing one year of continuous service.
non_obvious_actual_reality: While the law permits job changes after 1 year, the transfer requires both the current and new employer to have fully clean compliance records — no WPS violations, no MOL blacklisting. The process is not automatic: the new employer must sponsor a new residence permit and both employers' government accounts must be in good standing. Workers who attempt to change employers before completing 1 year without employer consent face permit cancellation and repatriation.
non_obvious_action_required: Before advising an employee to resign and accept a new role, confirm: (1) 1 full year of service is completed; (2) the new employer has available work permit quota and a clean MOL/MOI compliance status; (3) the employee's QID validity covers the transfer processing period of 2–4 weeks. Do not resign from current role until new sponsorship transfer is confirmed in writing.
source: Ministry of Labour Qatar — Labour Relations
